experiences.method_family: finite-scale positive surrogate gap -> positive root-normalized continuum gap inference
experiences.failure_mode: pointwise positivity of the dimensionless finite-scale gap, even uniform in volume at each fixed lattice spacing, can vanish after the required inverse-spacing physical normalization
residual_signature: r(a,L)=exp(-a^2) lies strictly between 0 and 1 for every a>0 and every L
dimensionless log-gap delta(a,L)=-log r(a,L)=a^2 is positive for every a and uniform in L
physical normalization delta(a,L)/a=a tends to 0 as a tends to 0
therefore fixed-a positivity alone does not imply a positive continuum physical liminf
broken_assumptions: positivity of a surrogate dimensionless gap at every cutoff is sufficient without a quantitative cutoff-scaled lower bound
scope_conditions: logical inference from pointwise positive finite-scale transfer-eigenvalue ratio gap to a positive inverse-spacing-normalized continuum gap
abstract positive sequences only; this record does not assert that the adversarial sequence is realized by Yang-Mills transfer matrices
competing_diagnoses: actual Yang-Mills dynamics may impose extra RG/positivity/locality structure excluding the adversarial sequence
uniformity in volume may be insufficient but a quantitative lower bound proportional to lattice spacing may repair the inference
the physically correct normalization or order of limits may differ for a concrete transfer-matrix setup and must be frozen target-specifically
experiences.selected_diagnosis: the weak bridge omits the quantitative lattice-spacing scaling needed to keep a finite positive physical gap through the continuum limit; the abstract inference is invalid, while the actual Yang-Mills bridge remains open
experiences.falsifier_or_attempt: set r(a,L)=exp(-a^2), independently of L, and compare the positive finite-a dimensionless gap -log r=a^2 with the physical normalization -a^{-1}log r=a
experiences.observed_result: the surrogate gap is positive for every cutoff and uniform in L, while the physical normalized gap tends to zero; hence pointwise finite-scale positivity cannot supply the YM-S1 continuum conclusion without a stronger scaled bridge
local_repair_attempts: replace pointwise positivity by an explicit target-specific condition such as liminf_{a->0} inf_L [-log r(a,L)]/a > 0 along the admissible scaling trajectory, with the correct order of limits
audit whether any cited lattice/RG theorem actually supplies the required uniform scaled bound rather than only fixed-cutoff positivity or correlation decay
